1.

2.

The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants seeking quashing of summoning o rder dated 6.4.2019 as well as entire proceeding of Complaint Case No.4838 of 2017 (Mahesh Pal Singh vs. Vipin Kumar and others) under Sections 498-A, 323 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Manth, District-Mathura, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Mathura.

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that during the pendency of the instant application,
since it was a matrimonial dispute between the applicant No.1 and daughter of opposite party No.2,
the said matrimonial dispute was amicably settled and the compromise was filed before the trial court concerned and on the basis of said compromise, the applicant No.1 had filed another Application u/S 482 Cr.P.C. No.34212 of 2022 and vide order dated 24.11.2022, this Court had directed the parties to appear before the trial court for verification of the compromise and the said compromise arrived at between the parties was verified vide order dated 4th January, 2023.
Thereupon, the proceedings of the aforesaid complaint case were quashed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 29.3.2023 passed in the aforesaid case, record of which has been produced along with the instant application as per the earlier orders passed by this Court.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that since the matrimonial dispute between the applicant and the daughter of opposite party No.2 has duly been settled amicably and on the basis of which proceedings have already been quashed, therefore, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the said complaint case against the applicants as well.

5. The order dated 29.3.2023 passed in Application u/S 482 Cr.P.C. No.34212 of 2022 (Vipin Kumar vs. State of UP and another) reads as under:
"Heard Mr.Digvijay Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, the learned Additional Government Advocate for the State as also perused the material available on record.
This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed challenging the summoning order dated 6th April, 2019 as well as the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No.
4838 of 2017 (Mahesh Pal Singh Vs. Vipin Kumar & Others), under Sections 498A,
323 I.P.C. as also under Sections 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Manth,
District-Mathura, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Mathura on the basis of compromise entered into between the parties.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the dispute between the parties, who are husband and wife, is purely matrimonial in nature.

sentences.text: The complaint case came to be filed by the opposite party no. 2 owing to some misunderstanding and misgivings between the parties and not on account of any real occurrence as alleged.
There never was any criminal intent on part of the applicant/s nor any criminal offence as alleged had ever occurred.
There are no injuries.
At present, the parties to the dispute who are related to each other, have resolved their differences and made peace.
In view of the settlement reached between the parties, they pray another chance be given to them to develop and experience normal relationship.
The continuance of the criminal trial may in fact hamper the otherwise good chance of the parties enjoying a normal relationship.
In such changed circumstances, the opposite party no. 2 does not wish to press charges against the applicant.
In the above regard, a compromise has been entered into between the parties.

Thereafter the applicants have approached this Court by means of the present application for quashing the aforesaid case in terms of compromise entered into Vipin Kumar And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65830635/
2 between the parties.

A Coordinate Bench of this Court passed following order on 24th November, 2022:
"Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed for quashing the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 4838 of 2017 (Mahesh Pal Singh Vs. Vipin Kumar and others)
under Sections 498A, 323 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Manth, District Mathura pending before learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, District Mathura as well as to quash the summoning order dated 06.04.2019 passed in the aforesaid case.

entities.text: Mahesh Pal Singh Vs. Vipin Kumar and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that by the efflux of time, the parties have reconciled their differences and a compromise has been entered between them which has been reduced in writing.

Accordingly, it is provided that the parties shall appear before the court below along with a certified copy of this order on the next date fixed and be permitted to file an application for verification of the original compromise document.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a date for the verification of the compromise entered into between the parties and pass an appropriate order with respect to the verification within a period of two months from today.
Upon due verification, the court below may pass appropriate order in that regard and send a report to this Court.

List after two months along with record of Criminal Misc. (482) Application No.
19478 of 2019.

Till then no coercive measure shall be taken against the applicant in the aforesaid case."
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that in compliance of the order of this Court dated 24th November, 2022, the court below has verified the said compromise vide order dated 4th January, 2023, copies of the compromise deed and verification order have been brought on record the order-sheet of the present application.

On the instruction received, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 submits that since the parties have entered into a compromise and the same has also been verified by the court below, opposite party no. 2 has no objection, if the proceedings in the aforesaid case are quashed.

This Court is not unmindful of the following judgements of the Apex Court:
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; (2003)4 SCC 675,
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2008) 9 SCC 677,

sentences.text: In the aforesaid judgments, the Apex Court has categorically held that compromise can be made between the parties even in respect of certain cognizable and non compoundable offences.

Reference may also be made to the decision given by this Court in Shaifullah and Others Vs. State of U.P. & Another; 2013 (83) ACC 278. in which the law expounded by the Apex court in the aforesaid cases has been explained in detail.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, the court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned complaint case as the parties have already settled their dispute.

Accordingly, the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 4838 of 2017 (Mahesh Pal Singh Vs. Vipin Kumar & Others), under Sections 498A, 323 I.P.C. as also under Sections 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Manth, District-Mathura, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Court No.3, Mathura , are hereby quashed.

7. Act, Police Station-Manth, District-Mathura, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Mathura,
